raw_response: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "Organizing pneumonia", "reason": "The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, patchy, peripheral, and subpleural airspace opacities (consolidations) in the mid-to-lower lung zones. This distribution is the classic radiological hallmark of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP). While Bronchioloalveolar carcinoma (A) can present similarly, OP is the prototypical diagnosis for this specific pattern of migratory or persistent peripheral consolidation. Sarcoidosis (C) typically presents with hilar adenopathy and upper lobe reticulonodular disease. Wegener's (D) usually shows nodules/cavities. TB (F) favors apical cavitation. The visual evidence strongly supports Organizing Pneumonia."}
